title: Start Programming From Zero
goal: Build the first working foundation in programming, web basics, GitHub, and small projects.
skipUntilLater: Do not start with advanced system design, cloud orchestration, or machine learning theory.
Avoid collecting dozens of courses before finishing one project-based path.
checkpoint: Build and publish a small personal site with at least one interactive feature and a README explaining what you learned.

title: Become a Frontend Developer
goal: Learn modern frontend fundamentals, UI implementation, framework basics, and production-quality web behavior.
skipUntilLater: Do not start by memorizing every framework API.
Delay advanced animation, micro-frontend, and build-system optimization until layout and JavaScript fundamentals are reliable.
checkpoint: Build a responsive dashboard from a design, pass basic accessibility checks, and deploy it with a short case-study README.

title: Become a Backend Developer
goal: Learn APIs, servers, databases, authentication-ready architecture, and operational basics.
skipUntilLater: Do not start with distributed systems before you can build and test a simple API.
Avoid premature microservices; first learn one service, one database, and one deployment.
checkpoint: Build a CRUD API with validation, tests, a PostgreSQL schema, Docker setup, and a short architecture note.

title: Build Full-Stack Projects
goal: Turn frontend, backend, database, deployment, and documentation skills into useful portfolio applications.
skipUntilLater: Do not start with complex SaaS billing, permissions, or multi-tenant architecture.
Avoid copying tutorial apps without changing the data model, UI, or workflow.
checkpoint: Ship one public project with authentication-ready structure, persistent data, CI validation, deployment, and a clear demo path.

title: Learn AI/ML Engineering
goal: Build practical data, machine learning, model discovery, and evaluation habits before moving into advanced research.
skipUntilLater: Do not start with fine-tuning large models before understanding datasets, evaluation, and basic Python workflows.
Avoid using model demos without recording inputs, outputs, limitations, and evaluation notes.
checkpoint: Create a small notebook or app that loads a dataset, runs a baseline model or hosted model, and documents evaluation limits.

title: Learn DevOps and Cloud
goal: Learn automation, containers, CI/CD, hosting, observability, and infrastructure discovery in a practical order.
skipUntilLater: Do not begin with multi-cluster Kubernetes operations.
Avoid cloud spending experiments until you understand free tiers, cleanup steps, and access controls.
checkpoint: Containerize a small app, run tests in GitHub Actions, deploy it, and add one basic metric or health check.

title: Learn Cybersecurity Safely
goal: Study defensive security, web risks, and lawful lab-style learning without drifting into unsafe or harmful material.
skipUntilLater: Do not test systems you do not own or have explicit permission to assess.
Avoid malware, credential theft, exploit trading, or anything that bypasses consent.
checkpoint: Review a demo application against OWASP guidance and write a defensive checklist with risks, fixes, and verification steps.

title: Prepare for Developer Interviews
goal: Build a focused interview preparation path across coding, frontend, system design, resume, and project explanation.
skipUntilLater: Do not grind random problems without reviewing patterns and mistakes.
Avoid over-optimizing resumes before you can explain one real project clearly.
checkpoint: Prepare one project walkthrough, solve and review a small set of tagged problems, and write notes for tradeoffs you can explain aloud.

title: Contribute to Open Source
goal: Learn the GitHub contribution workflow, find approachable issues, and make useful project contributions.
skipUntilLater: Do not start by rewriting project architecture or opening huge unfocused pull requests.
Avoid drive-by contributions that ignore maintainers' contribution rules.
checkpoint: Open one small, scoped pull request with a clear description, validation notes, and respectful follow-up on review feedback.

title: Find Tools for a New Project
goal: Choose useful APIs, hosting, deployment, CLI, automation, and documentation resources without overbuilding.
skipUntilLater: Do not add tools because they are popular; add them when the project has a concrete need.
Avoid paid infrastructure until the free tier, data limits, and exit path are clear.
checkpoint: Create a one-page project stack note that lists the chosen API, hosting path, CI check, deployment target, and why each was selected.
